info.title: Logging in and managing your &gnome; Desktop session

abstract.para: Learn how to log in to &gnome; Desktop and how to pause or finish the session.

section.title: Starting a session
section.para: When starting your system, you first see a login screen. All users must authenticate before starting a session. This step protects your personal information and data from unauthorized access.

step.para: In the login screen, select your user name.
If your user name is not listed, click Not listed?. Then enter your user name and click Next.
Enter your password and confirm with .

note.title: Enabling Automatic Login
note.para: If the computer is used by a single person, you can enable Automatic Login for this user at system start. This saves time, but also impacts account security. Enable or disable Automatic Login during installationa or in SettingsUsers: Select the account and switch on Automatic Login. Disable Automatic Login to maintain account security.

section.title: Pausing or finishing your session
section.para: To pause or end your session, open the System menu in the upper-right corner of the top bar. Click the Power Off button and choose one of the options:

formalpara.para: Pauses your session and puts the computer into a low-power mode. Suspend mode can be configured to lock your screen so nobody can view or change your work. Waking up the computer is generally much quicker than a full start.

listitem.para: This mode is also known as suspend-to-RAM, sleep or standby mode.

formalpara.para: Ends the current session and restarts the computer. A restart is required to apply updates that cannot be applied online, such as kernel, firmware or driver updates (see ).
Ends the current session and turns off the computer.
Ends the current session and returns to the login screen. This allows you (or another user) to log in again.
Keeps your current session active in the background while allowing another user to log in. You can return to your session later.

step.para: To lock the screen, open the System menu in the upper-right corner of the top bar and click the padlock icon.

result.para: When you lock your screen, a curtain with a clock appears first. After a while, the screen turns black.

step.para: To unlock the screen, move the mouse or press a key to display the locked screen dialog. Enter your password and press .

note.title: Option only available on multi-user systems
note.para: The Switch User option only appears in the menu if there is more than one user account on the system.

step.para: Open the System menu and click the Power Off button.
Select one of the following options:

listitem.para: Logs you out of the current session and returns to the login screen.
Keeps your session active in the background so another user can log in. You can return to your session later.

section.title: Restarting or shutting down the computer

step.para: Open the System menu and click the Power Off button.
Select one of the following options:

listitem.para: Logs you out of the current session, then restarts the system.
Logs you out of the current session, then shuts down the system.
